national_sources.name: the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP)

notes.inflation: Inflation is Peru's consumer price index for Metropolitan Lima, the headline measure, as the Central Reserve Bank of Peru publishes it: the change on twelve months, and on the previous month. The interest rate is the Central Reserve Bank of Peru's reference rate, shown from September 2003, when it became the bank's policy instrument.
notes.labour: Unemployment is the International Labour Organization's modelled annual estimate, published by the World Bank, not INEI's own survey figure. Real GDP is quarterly, from the Central Reserve Bank of Peru, in soles at 2007 prices and not seasonally adjusted, so quarters are compared with the same quarter a year earlier. GDP at current prices is annual, from the World Bank.
notes.trade: Goods trade is the Central Reserve Bank of Peru's monthly trade balance, in US dollars, converted to soles at each month's average exchange rate from the Bank for International Settlements. Both exports and imports are valued free on board.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are the IMF World Economic Outlook's general government figures, actual years only, so estimates and projections never appear as data.
notes.markets: The exchange rate is the World Bank's annual average official rate, shown from 1991, when the sol replaced the inti after the hyperinflation of the late 1980s. There is no 10-year government bond yield or business confidence index on this page.
